scenes.visual: COLOUR MAP (used in both films): 16:9, warm off-white background, flat cartoon style, no molecular structures. Paramecium = TEAL slipper-shaped cell with a fringe of short hairs (cilia). Food = AMBER dots (bacteria). Oxygen = CYAN dots; carbon dioxide = GREY dots. Water = PALE BLUE droplets. Wastes = BROWN specks. The JOB CHECKLIST is a white panel on the right with six icons in this order, each with a grey tick box: a running arrow 'move', a fork 'get food', two arrows in and out 'gas exchange', a bin with a droplet 'get rid of wastes and water', a lightning bolt 'respond', a cell splitting in two 'reproduce'. The FIVE LEVELS have fixed colours: cell = PURPLE, tissue = BLUE, organ = GREEN, organ system = ORANGE, organism = GOLD. Red blood cell = RED disc dented on both faces. Anything not computed from the lesson's numbers carries a small corner label 'schematic'. Title card 'One Cell, Every Job' fades in over a drop of pond water with a TEAL Paramecium drifting inside it.

scenes.tts: A Paramecium is one cell. You are made of about thirty trillion. You both do the same jobs, so why do you need so many cells?
scenes.caption: A Paramecium is one cell. You are made of about 30 trillion. You both do the same jobs, so why do you need so many cells?
scenes.visual: Split screen. Left: one TEAL Paramecium in a pond drop, label '1 cell'. Right: a cartoon student outline filled with a fine mesh of tiny cells, label 'about 30 trillion cells'. A large question mark rises between them.
scenes.narration: A Paramecium is one cell. You are made of about 30 trillion. You both do the same jobs, so why do you need so many cells?

scenes.tts: Both of you share one list of life jobs. You move, get food and exchange gases. You get rid of wastes and extra water. You respond to the world, and you reproduce.
scenes.visual: The JOB CHECKLIST panel slides in on the right. Each of the six icons lights in turn as its job is named, then dims to grey with an empty tick box. The pond drop with the Paramecium fills the left two thirds.
scenes.narration: Both of you share one list of life jobs. You move, get food and exchange gases. You get rid of wastes and extra water. You respond to the world, and you reproduce.

scenes.tts: Watch one Paramecium do every job on that list. Short, hair-like parts called cilia cover the whole cell. They beat together and push it through the water.
scenes.visual: Zoom into the TEAL Paramecium. Its fringe of cilia ripples in waves from front to back and the cell glides forward across the drop. The 'move' icon gets a tick.
scenes.narration: Watch one Paramecium do every job on that list. Short, hair-like parts called cilia cover the whole cell. They beat together and push it through the water.

scenes.tts: It sweeps bacteria into a groove on one side. They end up in small sacs called food vacuoles, where the food is digested.
scenes.visual: AMBER dots swirl into a groove on the cell's side. A small round sac pinches off around them and drifts inward; the AMBER dots inside fade as they are digested. Label 'food vacuole'. The 'get food' icon ticks.
scenes.narration: It sweeps bacteria into a groove on one side. They end up in small sacs called food vacuoles, where the food is digested.

scenes.tts: Oxygen passes in across its outer membrane. Carbon dioxide passes out the same way. No lungs, no gills, just the surface of one cell.
scenes.visual: The cell's outer edge is drawn as a thin line labelled 'outer membrane'. CYAN oxygen dots drift in across it; GREY carbon dioxide dots drift out. The 'gas exchange' icon ticks.
scenes.narration: Oxygen passes in across its outer membrane. Carbon dioxide passes out the same way. No lungs, no gills, just the surface of one cell.

scenes.tts: Pond water keeps moving into the cell. A sac called a contractile vacuole fills with the extra water and squeezes it out. Bits of food it cannot digest leave through a small opening.
scenes.visual: PALE BLUE droplets seep in all around the cell. A star-shaped sac swells with them, then squeezes and squirts them out. Near the rear, BROWN specks leave through a small opening. Labels 'contractile vacuole' and 'opening'. The 'get rid of wastes and water' icon ticks.
scenes.narration: Pond water keeps moving into the cell. A sac called a contractile vacuole fills with the extra water and squeezes it out. Bits of food it cannot digest leave through a small opening.

scenes.tts: When it bumps into something, it backs up, turns, and swims off another way. That is a response.
scenes.visual: The Paramecium swims into a grey sand grain, stops, reverses a short way, rotates, and swims off at a new angle; a dotted path traces the move. The 'respond' icon ticks.
scenes.narration: When it bumps into something, it backs up, turns, and swims off another way. That is a response.

scenes.tts: And it can divide. It pinches in the middle and becomes two cells. Every job is done inside one cell, with different parts helping.
scenes.visual: The cell narrows at its middle and splits into two TEAL Paramecia that swim apart. The 'reproduce' icon ticks; all six ticks now glow on the checklist.
scenes.narration: And it can divide. It pinches in the middle and becomes two cells. Every job is done inside one cell, with different parts helping.

scenes.tts: So why not keep one cell and make it bigger? Could one cell grow as big as you and still do every job? Pause and decide.
scenes.visual: One TEAL cell sits centred with a grey outline of a human body traced around it, much larger. The words 'Pause and predict' appear.
scenes.narration: So why not keep one cell and make it bigger? Could one cell grow as big as you and still do every job? Pause and decide.

scenes.visual: Hold on the small cell inside the large body outline; a thin countdown bar shrinks along the bottom.

scenes.tts: Not by just growing bigger in every direction. Food and oxygen must cross the cell’s surface, its outer membrane, to get in. Carbon dioxide and many wastes pass out across it.
scenes.visual: A plain round cell (schematic) replaces the Paramecium. Its outer membrane is drawn as a ring of small doors. AMBER and CYAN dots stream in through the doors toward the middle; GREY carbon dioxide dots and some BROWN specks stream out.
scenes.narration: Not by just growing bigger in every direction. Food and oxygen must cross the cell’s surface, its outer membrane, to get in. Carbon dioxide and many wastes pass out across it.

scenes.tts: Now let the cell grow, but keep its shape. Its inside grows faster than its surface, and its middle gets farther away. Without special features, a big enough cell may not get food and oxygen to its middle fast enough.
scenes.visual: The round cell swells to several times its width, keeping the same round shape (schematic; corner label 'same shape'). On screen: 'surface: x4  inside: x8' for one doubling. The incoming dots slow and stop short of the centre; the centre fades from white to grey. Label 'middle falls behind'.
scenes.narration: Now let the cell grow, but keep its shape. Its inside grows faster than its surface, and its middle gets farther away. Without special features, a big enough cell may not get food and oxygen to its middle fast enough.

scenes.tts: So your big body is not one giant cell. It is made of many small cells. Each one sits close to the watery fluid that brings it food and oxygen.
scenes.visual: The swollen grey cell breaks into a tight cluster of many small round cells with thin channels of PALE BLUE fluid between them. AMBER and CYAN dots flow along the channels and reach every small cell; every cell stays white.
scenes.narration: So your big body is not one giant cell. It is made of many small cells. Each one sits close to the watery fluid that brings it food and oxygen.

scenes.tts: Many cells bring a second gain. They can split up the job list. Different groups of cells can take on different jobs.
scenes.visual: The six checklist icons lift off the panel and float over the cluster. Each icon settles over its own group of cells, and that group takes on a tint (schematic). The rest of the cluster stays plain.
scenes.narration: Many cells bring a second gain. They can split up the job list. Different groups of cells can take on different jobs.

scenes.tts: Sharing the work this way is called division of labor. A Paramecium does the whole list in one small cell. You do the same list with trillions of small cells that share it.
scenes.visual: Banner 'division of labor'. Split screen again: left, one TEAL Paramecium with all six ticks; right, the student outline whose mesh of tiny cells shows the six group tints.
scenes.narration: Sharing the work this way is called division of labor. A Paramecium does the whole list in one small cell. You do the same list with trillions of small cells that share it.

scenes.visual: End card with the Hex mascot holding a small TEAL cell. Take-home line: 'Grow a cell in every direction, and its surface falls behind.'
